mechanisms.name: Post-quantum registry encryption
mechanisms.build: ML-KEM-768 for key establishment, hybrid with X25519; AES-256-GCM at rest over the expert-id to identity map; the key is held by the committee service
mechanisms.guarantees: Long-horizon confidentiality of the identity map against harvest-now-decrypt-later
mechanisms.does_not: Confidentiality from an administrator with the key; anything about answers

mechanisms.name: Post-quantum outcome attestations
mechanisms.build: ML-DSA-65 signs each resolved ledger entry (risk_id, outcome, resolved_at, round commitment root); the public key is published on the ledger
mechanisms.guarantees: The outcome record was issued by the committee key and has not been altered since
mechanisms.does_not: Truth of the outcome; anything about who answered

mechanisms.name: Blind-signed single-use credentials
mechanisms.build: RSA blind signatures (RFC 9474 RSABSSA-SHA384-PSS-Deterministic): the committee signs a blinded token per pulse allowance, the expert unblinds it and spends one token per answer; the server verifies the signature and rejects reuse by nullifier
mechanisms.where_it_shows: Expert card under the anonymous mask; committee view: tokens issued and spent, never linked
mechanisms.guarantees: A vetted panel member answered, unlinkable by the committee to the approval
mechanisms.does_not: Protection against timing or network-metadata correlation; re-identification by distinctive wording

mechanisms.name: Zero-knowledge group membership
mechanisms.build: Semaphore-v4-shaped group per panel with a per-pulse nullifier. The group root and the nullifier registry are built and enforced; the Groth16 proof check itself is NOT implemented in this build, which is why the flag ships off
mechanisms.where_it_shows: Round view: the proof line, which says what was and was not checked
mechanisms.guarantees: Double-answer prevention by nullifier, enforced server-side
mechanisms.does_not: Membership without identity -- that needs the proof verifier this build does not have; reputation portability; not required for the pilot design

mechanisms.name: Public timestamp
mechanisms.build: A daily Merkle root of that day's commitments is signed and entered into Sigstore Rekor, a public append-only transparency log; the entry, signed timestamp and inclusion proof are stored, and the status stays pending until the log returns the proof
mechanisms.where_it_shows: Ledger: timestamp status per day; Verify shows the root, the log index and a link to the public entry
mechanisms.guarantees: Independent proof the commitments existed by that time, once the status reads anchored
mechanisms.does_not: Who answered, or whether an answer is right; nothing but the root is logged. A pending root proves nothing yet

mechanisms.name: Registry access log
mechanisms.build: Every read of the identity map is logged with who, when and why
mechanisms.guarantees: Committee access to identities is defined and visible
mechanisms.does_not: Prevention of access by an authorised administrator

mechanisms.name: End-to-end answer encryption
mechanisms.build: The expert card encrypts the answer in the browser: ML-KEM-768 hybrid with X25519, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, to a key pair only the engine holds; the token and route are bound into the ciphertext
mechanisms.where_it_shows: Expert card: the line under the receipt
mechanisms.guarantees: The answer is readable only by the engine; a CDN, proxy or tunnel in between cannot read it or alter it undetected
mechanisms.does_not: Hiding the answer from the operator of the engine; protecting a compromised device or browser

registry.key_holder: committee service (this process, in the pilot)
registry.lock_line: Identity map encrypted with ML-KEM-768 + X25519 hybrid, AES-256-GCM, key held by the committee.
registry.guarantees: Long-horizon confidentiality of the identity map against harvest-now-decrypt-later
registry.does_not: Confidentiality from an administrator with the key; anything about answers

attestation_key.note: FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 verification key. Anyone holding it can check an attestation without this service.

issuer.note: Generated at process start: `cryptography` has no seeded RSA keygen, so a restart publishes a new issuer and retires every token signed by the old one.

credentials.linkage_note: 1 of 36 tokens were blinded by the card and are unlinkable to their approval. The other 35 came from the demo path and are not.
credentials.guarantees: A vetted panel member answered, unlinkable by the committee to the approval
credentials.does_not: Protection against timing or network-metadata correlation; re-identification by distinctive wording

zk.guarantees: Double-answer prevention by nullifier, enforced server-side
zk.does_not: Membership without identity -- that needs the proof verifier this build does not have; reputation portability; not required for the pilot design

calibration.means: Counts only. A report belongs to the expert, and reaches the committee only if that expert says yes a second time.
